findings:
🔵 [cost-tracker-sink-no-fallback] CUT/FOLLOW-UP hooks/cost-tracker.js:201-205 ignores the writeAdvisory() return in sink mode. If the live dir is unwritable, the queued advice reaches neither the band nor the relay; only the stderr copy remains. hooks/context-budget.js emitT1 instead falls back to injection when the write fails. Optional parity: fall through to the advisory-queue branch when writeAdvisory returns false. Excluded because P7a only requires the stderr copy to remain, and it does.
🔵 [advisory-trim-race] CUT/FOLLOW-UP hooks/_shared/advisory-sink.js:66-73 trims with read → tmp → rename, outside any lock. A concurrent append from another hook in the same session that lands between the read and the rename is dropped. The file stays bounded (256 KiB / 100 rows) and the rename is atomic, so readers never see a torn file. Excluded because the trim is documented as best-effort and the only effect is a rare lost toast.
🔵 [review-test-dev-shm] CUT/FOLLOW-UP scripts/review-input.test.js:141 hard-codes /dev/shm for the live dir, which does not exist on macOS. Optional: fall back to os.tmpdir() when /dev/shm is missing. Excluded because the repo's live dir is tmpfs-by-design and this host is Linux.
